title: Recsys · serving
description: The orchestrator's five stages against their budgets, the funnel, the four named degradations, arm balance, feature drift and the impression log. Every threshold here mirrors serving/monitoring/alerts.yml, so a red panel and a firing alert cannot disagree. TWO scrape jobs: recsys-orchestrator at recsys-host:9102 (the host, via $HOST_IP) and recsys-drift at drift:9103 (in the compose network). A drift panel reading No data while the latency panels are fine means the second target is down, not that nothing drifted -- check /api/v1/targets before believing either.

panels.title: p99 end to end
panels.description: RecsysP99OverBudget fires past 100ms for 5m. The 90ms figure in docs/design.md is the BUDGET; the alert sits at 100ms so a brief excursion is not a page.

panels.title: Fallback rate
panels.description: Share of OK slates that are the popularity list. RecsysFallbackRate pages past 5%. A healthy-looking service at 97% fallback is the exact failure Part M's first run hit.

panels.title: Server error rate
panels.description: RecsysErrorRate pages past 1%. InvalidArgument is excluded here and tracked on its own, because a malformed-request spike is a caller bug, not an outage. The numerator is `or vector(0)`-ed: recsys_requests_total is labelled by code, so with no errors the selector matches NO series and sum() over nothing is empty, not zero -- which Grafana renders as 'No data', indistinguishable from the metric having disappeared.

panels.title: Feature store age
panels.description: Seconds behind the stalest materialised Feast view, from the gateway's readiness probe. 0 means no reading yet, NOT fresh. §16.1 wants an alert past 10 minutes. ⚠️ ON MIND THIS READS ~7 YEARS AND IS CORRECT: the corpus's event timestamps are from 2019 and this is measured against wall-clock now. Same event-time-vs-wall-clock gap as the retention.ms=-1 decision in make/kafka.mk. The §16.1 alert therefore CANNOT be enabled on this corpus without either measuring against the corpus's own max timestamp or pinning a reference clock -- an unresolved decision, not a panel bug.

panels.title: Per-stage p99, against each stage's budget
panels.description: ONE axis: budgets and measurements are both seconds. Dashed grey is the budget, built with the same label_replace(vector(...)) construction RecsysStageOverBudget uses. Stage colours are fixed per stage, so hiding a series never repaints the others.

targets.expr:
label_replace(vector(0.008), "stage", "features",  "", "")
or label_replace(vector(0.025), "stage", "retrieval", "", "")
or label_replace(vector(0.035), "stage", "rank",      "", "")
or label_replace(vector(0.005), "stage", "rerank",    "", "")

panels.title: End to end, three quantiles
panels.description: One hue, light to dark: these are three magnitudes of the same measure, not three entities. The dashed line is the 90ms whole-system budget from docs/design.md.

panels.title: Median candidates surviving each stage
panels.description: A funnel is magnitude across ordered stages, so bars beat lines. ONE QUERY PER STAGE, in pipeline order, which is the whole reason for four targets: a single `by (stage)` query returns series sorted ALPHABETICALLY, so the bars read retrieved/scored/served/unblocked, and a funnel whose bars are out of order is not conveying a funnel. unblocked below 1 for 10m is RecsysSeenFilterSaturated: the seen-list is blocking everything. incomplete_rows is not a funnel stage and lives on the degradation panel.

panels.title: Degradation, as a share of OK traffic
panels.description: Every one of these returned 200. RecsysRankerDegraded and RecsysFeatureGatewayDegraded page past 2%; the fallback rate pages past 5%. Read this before believing any quality number.

panels.title: Assignments per arm
panels.description: The SRM input. `none` is the unassigned arm and is counted on purpose: a holdback that is not counted makes the chi-square compare arms against a denominator it cannot see.

panels.title: Arm imbalance
panels.description: max/min assignment rate across arms over 30m, excluding `none`. RecsysExperimentImbalance tickets past 1.2. If this fires the experiment is INVALID whatever the primary metric did.

panels.title: Served score distribution
panels.description: The PSI input. A HISTOGRAM, not a summary: PSI is computed between two distributions and needs the same bucket edges on both sides, and quantiles cannot be re-bucketed after the fact. Buckets are LinearBuckets(-10, 1, 21).

panels.title: Feature drift (PSI) against training's bins
panels.description: Served user features against the bins the model was FITTED on, read from serving/artifacts/drift_baseline.json. The dashed line at 0.25 is common.drift.PSI_SKEW -- the same number RecsysFeatureDrift fires on and the same band docs/skew_report.md calls SKEW, and tests/test_drift_window.py asserts the three agree rather than leaving it to a comment. Dashed grey is a feature in EXPECTED_CHURN: shown, never paged on, because on a news corpus a naive PSI alarm fires constantly and then gets muted. That set is EMPTY today -- ImpressionContext carries user_feats only, so no item feature reaches this panel at all. NO SERIES APPEARS BELOW 500 ROWS: the monitor reports nothing rather than a confident number off forty requests, which is what the window panel beside this is for.

panels.title: Drift window
panels.description: Rows in the monitor's rolling window. Below 500 it reports NO PSI at all, and RecsysDriftMonitorStarved tickets after 30m there. That is a SEPARATE alert from the PSI one on purpose: a series that does not exist cannot breach a threshold, so an absent PSI would otherwise be silent for as long as the monitor saw no traffic. Zero while the endpoint is up does NOT on its own mean an idle topic: a record is also declined when its feature fetch had already failed, when the store held no row for that user, and when its width disagrees with the baseline. Read the outcome panel below before concluding anything from a zero here.

panels.title: User rows found
panels.description: Share of non-degraded requests that had a stored user row. A SEPARATE number from the distributions above and deliberately not pooled into them: a store miss serves zeros and training fills a missing row with zeros too, so pooling would let the miss RATE masquerade as a shift in the values. Train coverage on this corpus is 66.7% (docs/skew_report.md), so a served figure far off that is worth reading before any PSI on this row. Renders No data rather than 0% when no request was eligible, because nothing that never reached a feature fetch can have missed one: 0% would read as "every request missed", which is a measurement, and nothing was measured.

panels.title: Drift records, by outcome
panels.description: Why the window is the size it is. seen is every record consumed since the monitor started. found is the subset that reached the window; degraded and malformed are the two refused for a stated reason; and seen minus all three is the store misses -- a user the feature store does not hold. Four readings: a flat seen is no impression_context traffic, or a dead consumer; seen climbing with degraded alongside it is the orchestrator losing its feature fetch, which is an availability incident and NOT skew; seen climbing with found flat and degraded flat is a feature store holding no row for these users; malformed above zero is a baseline whose width disagrees with the served vector, so re-dump it. Cumulative since start, so the slope is the rate and a drop to zero is a restart.

panels.title: Records lost, by cause
panels.description: Three causes, three fixes. dropped = the buffer was full or Serialize failed (raise -impression-buffer, or look at the registry). unmapped = item_map.json and the index disagree. undelivered = librdkafka accepted it and the broker never did. A clean `dropped` with a climbing `undelivered` is the broker, and only this panel can tell you that.
